description:
Technical Administrator

We're working with a leading design-led brand in the luxury interiors sector to find a Technical Administrator for their R&D team. A British business founded in the late 1990s, they now sell in over 90 countries with subsidiaries in the US and Asia. Behind every product that ships is a technical file that has to be complete, current and correct. That's what you'd own.

The Role

Reporting to the Technical Manager, you'll build and maintain product technical files in line with UK, European and North American regulations, supporting development teams in the UK and China. You'll work day-to-day in a Product Lifecycle Management system alongside Excel, covering specification records, engineering data, costings and quotations. You'll also own the Product Release Order process that takes a new product through to production release.

On top of that, you'll produce the weekly NPD report the Head of Product Development runs the meeting from, plus the monthly KPI report and carbon data.

Being Straight With You

This is an admin role, and it's meant to be. It isn't a route into engineering. But it's the role everything else leans on: if the data's wrong, products don't release and reports don't work.

You'll also spend a fair bit of time chasing engineers. They're busy, and admin isn't always their first port of call, so you need to be confident enough to keep asking and persuasive enough to get what you need.

What We're Looking For
- A couple of years in admin, ideally in a technical or engineering setting
- Intermediate Excel, including pivot tables and VLOOKUPs, and confident with exported data
- Very close attention to detail
- Confident and persuasive, comfortable chasing people
- Someone who enjoys owning the data and running a tight ship
- Proactive and positive, and genuinely happy doing admin
- ERP or PLM experience (SAP, NetSuite, Navision, Oracle) is an advantage

Why This One
- Real visibility. Your reports run the meetings, and your process releases the products
- Full ownership of product data across a global range
- A premium brand where detail is taken seriously at every level
- Full time, UK based, competitive salary and benefits

Behind every product that ships is a technical file that has to be complete, current and correct. That's what you'd own.

The Role

Reporting to the Technical Manager, you'll build and maintain product technical files in line with UK, European and North American regulations, supporting development teams in the UK and China. You'll work day-to-day in a Product Lifecycle Management system alongside Excel, covering specification records, engineering data, costings and quotations. This is an admin role, and it's meant to be. It isn't a route into engineering. But it's the role everything else leans on: if the data's wrong, products don't release and reports don't work.

You'll also spend a fair bit of time chasing engineers. They're busy, and admin isn't always their first port of call, so you need to be confident enough to keep asking and persuasive enough to get what you need.

- A couple of years in admin, ideally in a technical or engineering setting

This is an excellent opportunity to develop skills, gain experience, and make a positive difference in supporting people on their recovery journey.

About the Role

As a Recovery Coordinator, you will play a vital role in supporting individuals aged 18 and over who are experiencing drug and alcohol-related challenges. Working within an integrated healthcare framework, you will deliver person-centred psychosocial interventions that empower individuals to make positive, sustainable changes and work towards their recovery goals.

You will manage a caseload of service users, undertaking comprehensive assessments, developing risk management plans and creating SMART care plans tailored to each individual's needs. Using a flexible approach that combines harm reduction and abstinence-based interventions, you will provide practical advice, guidance and structured support to help individuals improve their health, wellbeing and quality of life.

Your responsibilities will include delivering structured one-to-one interventions, facilitating group-work sessions and supporting structured treatment programmes. You will use motivational interviewing techniques to engage service users, encourage positive behaviour change and promote long-term recovery.

Building effective partnerships with housing providers, employment services, healthcare professionals, probation, the criminal justice sector and other community organisations will be essential to ensuring continuity of care and addressing the wider needs of the people you support.

You will contribute to service performance targets and positive outcomes, working collaboratively with colleagues, partner agencies and local commissioners to deliver high-quality, recovery-focused services. You will also maintain accurate records, participate in clinical supervision and ensure that safeguarding, equality, diversity and inclusion are embedded in your practice.

Flexibility is important, as the role may occasionally require evening or weekend working, with reasonable notice, to meet service user needs and maintain continuity of care.

About You

You are a compassionate, motivated and recovery-focused professional with experience of working within substance misuse services and a genuine commitment to helping people achieve meaningful, lasting change. You understand that recovery is different for everyone and can adapt your approach to meet individual needs, whether through harm reduction, abstinence-based support or a combination of both.

You will bring experience of conducting comprehensive assessments, developing risk management plans and implementing SMART care plans, alongside the ability to deliver structured psychosocial interventions and facilitate both individual and group sessions. You will be confident using motivational interviewing techniques to build trusting relationships, encourage engagement and support service users to take ownership of their recovery.

You will also have:
- A sound understanding of substance misuse, addiction, the recovery agenda and the challenges faced by individuals affected by drug and alcohol use.
- A thorough knowledge of, and commitment to, the 12-step process of recovery from addiction.
- An understanding of safeguarding, risk management, equality, diversity and inclusion, and the importance of delivering safe, accessible and person-centred services.
- Knowledge of community support services, holistic care needs and the importance of effective throughcare and continuity of care.
- An understanding of the criminal justice sector and the needs of individuals accessing support in community or prison settings.
- Experience of working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams and external partner agencies to improve outcomes for service users.
- Strong IT, communication, organisational and record-keeping skills, with the ability to manage a caseload effectively and work towards agreed targets.
- An understanding of NHS health and wellbeing outcomes and the importance of measuring progress and demonstrating positive results.
- A commitment to reflective practice, professional development and making effective use of clinical supervision.

Above all, you will be non-judgemental, resilient and empathetic, with the ability to build positive relationships with people from diverse backgrounds. You will be passionate about promoting recovery, reducing harm, tackling health inequalities and helping individuals develop the confidence, skills and support networks they need to move forward with their lives.

About Us

We are The Forward Trust, the social enterprise with charitable status that empowers people to break the often interlinked cycles of crime and addiction to move forward with their lives. For more than 25 years we have been working with people to build positive and productive lives, whatever their past. We believe that anyone is capable of lasting change. Our services have supported thousands of people to make positive changes and build productive lives with a job, family, friends and a sense of community.

There's plenty of variety, and you'll be working with different people throughout the day. The important thing is making sure nothing gets missed and that each process is followed through to completion.
